question: One of the following statements about the epidemiology and prognosis of heart failure is INCORRECT. Point it out

options.opa: Between 60 and 70% of patients die in the first 5 years after establishing the diagnosis of heart failure.
options.opb: The functional situation of the patient with heart failure is the one that best correlates with the expectation of survival.
options.opc: Diastolic dysfunction predominates in elderly women with a history of chronic hypertension.
options.opd: Heart failure due to systolic dysfunction is usually observed in male patients with ischemic heart disease.
options.ope: The prevalence of heart failure is decreasing in the last decade thanks to better control of cardiovascular risk factors.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Functional status" -> "correlates with survival" -> "consistent with clinical observations" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Elderly women" -> "chronic hypertension" -> "diastolic dysfunction predominance" -> "consistent with epidemiology" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Systolic dysfunction" -> "male patients" -> "ischemic heart disease" -> "common association" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Prevalence of heart failure" -> "decreasing" -> "better control of risk factors" -> "inconsistent with current data" -> 70%
analysis: The statement that the prevalence of heart failure is decreasing in the last decade is incorrect. While there have been improvements in the management of cardiovascular risk factors, the prevalence of heart failure has not shown a clear decreasing trend. In fact, due to an aging population and improved survival from other cardiovascular conditions, the prevalence of heart failure is generally considered to be stable or increasing.
